name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q01 - Structure of glycogen similar to amylopectin

questiontext.text: Glycogen is a branched chain polymer of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose units in which chain is formed by C1—C4 glycosidic linkage whereas branching occurs by the formation of C1-C6 glycosidic linkage. Structure of glycogen is similar to

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Polysaccharides of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose differ in their chain architecture and degree of branching. Linear chains are formed via \(\text{C}1\text{--}\text{C}4\) \(\alpha\)-glycosidic linkages, whereas branching occurs through \(\text{C}1\text{--}\text{C}6\) \(\alpha\)-glycosidic linkages.

Step 2: Evaluation of Structures
Amylose is an unbranched, linear polymer of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose units joined solely by \(\text{C}1\text{--}\text{C}4\) glycosidic linkages. Cellulose is a linear polymer of \(\beta\)-D-glucose units joined by \(\text{C}1\text{--}\text{C}4\) \(\beta\)-glycosidic linkages. Glucose is a monosaccharide unit rather than a polymer. Amylopectin, like glycogen, is a branched-chain polymer of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose units containing \(\text{C}1\text{--}\text{C}4\) glycosidic linkages in the main chain and \(\text{C}1\text{--}\text{C}6\) glycosidic linkages at the branching points (with glycogen being even more extensively branched).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the structure of glycogen is similar to amylopectin.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q02 - Polymer stored in the liver of animals

questiontext.text: Which of the following polymer is stored in the liver of animals?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Animals store reserve carbohydrates in the form of a highly branched polysaccharide of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose known as animal starch.

Step 2: Evaluation
Amylose and amylopectin are components of plant starch, and cellulose is a structural polysaccharide found in plant cell walls. Glycogen is stored primarily in the liver and muscles of animals and is broken down by enzymes into glucose whenever the body requires energy.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, glycogen is the polymer stored in the liver of animals.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q03 - Hydrolysis products of one sucrose molecule

questiontext.text: Sucrose (cane sugar) is a disaccharide. One molecule of sucrose on hydrolysis gives

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Disaccharides are carbohydrates that yield two monosaccharide units upon acid-catalysed or enzymatic hydrolysis.

Step 2: Evaluation
Sucrose (\(\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}\)) is composed of one \(\alpha\)-D-glucopyranose unit and one \(\beta\)-D-fructofuranose unit linked by a glycosidic bond between \(\text{C}1\) of glucose and \(\text{C}2\) of fructose. On hydrolysis with dilute acid or the enzyme invertase, one molecule of sucrose yields equimolar amounts of D-(+)-glucose and D-(-)-fructose:

\[\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\ (\text{D-glucose}) + \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\ (\text{D-fructose})\]

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, one molecule of sucrose on hydrolysis gives 1 molecule of glucose and 1 molecule of fructose.

answer.text: 2 molecules of glucose + 1 molecule of fructose
1 molecule of glucose + 1 molecule of fructose

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q04 - Identifying pair of anomers from Fischer structures

questiontext.text: Which of the following pairs represents anomers?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Four pairs of monosaccharide structures are provided: two pairs of open-chain Fischer projections and two pairs of cyclic Fischer hemiacetal projections of aldohexoses.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In cyclic Fischer projections of D-aldohexoses, the anomeric carbon is \(\text{C}1\) (the hemiacetal carbon). In the \(\alpha\)-anomer, the \(-\text{OH}\) group at \(\text{C}1\) is on the right, whereas in the \(\beta\)-anomer, the \(-\text{OH}\) group at \(\text{C}1\) is on the left.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Anomers are cyclic stereoisomers of a sugar that differ in configuration exclusively at the hemiacetal or hemiketal carbon (the anomeric carbon, \(\text{C}1\) in aldoses).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
The first open-chain pair consists of D-glucose and D-mannose, which are \(\text{C}2\) epimers, not cyclic anomers. The second open-chain pair consists of D-glucose and L-glucose, which are enantiomers. The fourth pair consists of cyclic \(\alpha\)-D-glucose and \(\beta\)-L-glucose, which differ in configuration at \(\text{C}1, \text{C}2, \text{C}3,\) and \(\text{C}4\), so they are not anomers. The third pair consists of cyclic \(\alpha\)-D-glucopyranose (with \(-\text{OH}\) on the right at \(\text{C}1\)) and \(\beta\)-D-glucopyranose (with \(-\text{OH}\) on the left at \(\text{C}1\)), having identical configurations at \(\text{C}2, \text{C}3, \text{C}4,\) and \(\text{C}5\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since the cyclic structures of \(\alpha\)-D-glucopyranose and \(\beta\)-D-glucopyranose differ only in the configuration at the anomeric carbon \(\text{C}1\), they represent a pair of anomers.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q05 - Stabilisation of alpha-helix secondary structure of proteins

questiontext.text: Proteins are found to have two different types of secondary structures viz. \(\alpha\)-helix and \(\beta\)-pleated sheet structure. \(\alpha\)-helix structure of protein is stabilised by:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The secondary structure of a protein refers to the regular local folding of the polypeptide backbone into shapes such as the \(\alpha\)-helix and \(\beta\)-pleated sheet.

Step 2: Evaluation
In the \(\alpha\)-helix structure, the polypeptide chain twists into a right-handed screw-like helix. This helical conformation is stabilised by intramolecular hydrogen bonds formed between the \(-\text{NH}-\) group of each amino acid residue and the \(-\text{C=O}\) group of an adjacent turn of the helix (specifically four residues away).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the \(\alpha\)-helix structure of a protein is stabilised by hydrogen bonds.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q06 - Identifying non-reducing disaccharide from Haworth structures

questiontext.text: In disaccharides, if the reducing groups of monosaccharides i.e. aldehydic or ketonic groups are bonded, these are non-reducing sugars. Which of the following disaccharide is a non-reducing sugar?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Four Haworth projections of disaccharides are given: three consist of two six-membered pyranose rings linked between \(\text{C}1\) of the left ring and \(\text{C}4\) of the right ring, and one consists of an \(\alpha\)-D-glucopyranose ring linked to a \(\beta\)-D-fructofuranose ring.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In a pyranose ring, \(\text{C}1\) is the anomeric (hemiacetal) carbon. In a furanose ring of fructose, \(\text{C}2\) is the anomeric (hemiketal) carbon.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
A disaccharide is non-reducing if and only if both anomeric carbons are involved in the glycosidic linkage, leaving no free hemiacetal or hemiketal \(-\text{OH}\) group capable of opening to an aldehyde or ketone.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
In the three disaccharides with \(1,4\)-glycosidic linkages (maltose, lactose, and cellobiose), the \(\text{C}1\) anomeric carbon of the right-hand pyranose unit retains a free hemiacetal \(-\text{OH}\) group, making them reducing sugars. In contrast, the disaccharide consisting of \(\alpha\)-D-glucopyranose and \(\beta\)-D-fructofuranose (sucrose) has a glycosidic linkage between \(\text{C}1\) of glucose and \(\text{C}2\) of fructose. Because both reducing groups are bonded in the glycosidic linkage, there is no free hemiacetal or hemiketal group.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Therefore, the disaccharide formed by \(\alpha\)-D-glucopyranose and \(\beta\)-D-fructofuranose linked at \(\text{C}1\) and \(\text{C}2\) (sucrose) is a non-reducing sugar.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q07 - Identifying ascorbic acid as a vitamin

questiontext.text: Which of the following acids is a vitamin?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vitamins are essential organic micronutrients required in small amounts in the diet to perform specific biological functions.

Step 2: Evaluation
Aspartic acid is a non-essential \(\alpha\)-amino acid. Adipic acid is a dicarboxylic acid used in the manufacture of nylon-6,6. Saccharic acid is a dicarboxylic acid obtained by the oxidation of glucose with concentrated nitric acid. Ascorbic acid is the chemical name for Vitamin C, a water-soluble vitamin whose deficiency causes scurvy.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, ascorbic acid is a vitamin.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q08 - Carbon atoms involved in phosphodiester linkage of dinucleotide

questiontext.text: Dinucleotide is obtained by joining two nucleotides together by phosphodiester linkage. Between which carbon atoms of pentose sugars of nucleotides are these linkages present?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Nucleotides are the monomeric units of nucleic acids, each consisting of a pentose sugar, a nitrogenous base, and a phosphate group attached to the \(5^{\prime}\)-carbon of the sugar.

Step 2: Evaluation
When two nucleotides join to form a dinucleotide, the phosphate group attached to the \(5^{\prime}\)-carbon of one pentose sugar forms an ester bond with the \(-\text{OH}\) group at the \(3^{\prime}\)-carbon of the adjacent pentose sugar. This creates a \(5^{\prime}\text{--}3^{\prime}\) phosphodiester linkage.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the phosphodiester linkage is present between the \(5^{\prime}\) and \(3^{\prime}\) carbon atoms of the pentose sugars.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q09 - Monomeric units of nucleic acids

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) are long-chain polynucleotides.

Step 2: Evaluation
A sugar linked to a nitrogenous base forms a nucleoside. When a nucleoside is esterified with a phosphoric acid group at the \(5^{\prime}\) position, it forms a nucleotide. Repeating nucleotide units linked by \(3^{\prime}\text{--}5^{\prime}\) phosphodiester bonds constitute nucleic acids.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, nucleic acids are polymers of nucleotides.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q10 - Identifying incorrect statement about glucose structure

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements is not true about glucose?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Glucose (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\)) is an aldohexose that predominantly exists in a six-membered cyclic hemiacetal form.

Step 2: Evaluation of Properties
Glucose contains an aldehyde group and six carbon atoms, so it is an aldohexose. On prolonged heating with \(\text{HI}\), it forms \(n\)-hexane, confirming that all six carbon atoms are linked in a straight chain. Because its aldehyde group is involved in cyclic hemiacetal formation, glucose does not give the 2,4-DNP test. However, in its cyclic hemiacetal structure, the oxygen bridge forms between \(\text{C}1\) and \(\text{C}5\), resulting in a six-membered pyranose ring, not a five-membered furanose ring.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the statement that glucose is present in furanose form is not true.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q11 - Specific sequence of amino acids as primary structure

questiontext.text: Each polypeptide in a protein has aminoacids linked with each other in a specific sequence. This sequence of amino acids is said to be

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Protein structure is classified into four hierarchical levels: primary, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary.

Step 2: Evaluation
The primary structure of a protein is defined as the exact linear sequence in which amino acids are linked together by peptide bonds in a polypeptide chain. Secondary structure refers to local regular folding (\(\alpha\)-helix or \(\beta\)-sheet), tertiary structure describes the overall three-dimensional folding of a single polypeptide, and quaternary structure refers to the spatial arrangement of two or more polypeptide subunits.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the specific sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide is called the primary structure of proteins.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q12 - Nitrogenous base absent in RNA

questiontext.text: DNA and RNA contain four bases each. Which of the following bases is not present in RNA?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
DNA and RNA each contain two purine bases and two pyrimidine bases.

Step 2: Evaluation
Both DNA and RNA contain adenine, guanine, and cytosine. As the fourth base, DNA contains thymine, whereas RNA contains uracil instead of thymine.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, thymine is not present in RNA.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q13 - B group vitamin stored in human body

questiontext.text: Which of the following B group vitamins can be stored in our body?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vitamins are classified into fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K), which are stored in the liver and adipose tissues, and water-soluble vitamins (B group and C), which are generally excreted in urine and cannot be stored in the body.

Step 2: Evaluation
Vitamins \(\text{B}_1\), \(\text{B}_2\), and \(\text{B}_6\) are water-soluble and must be supplied regularly in the diet because they are not stored in significant amounts. Vitamin \(\text{B}_{12}\) is the notable exception among water-soluble B-group vitamins, as it can be stored in the human body (primarily in the liver).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, Vitamin \(\mathbf{B}_{12}\) can be stored in our body.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q14 - Nitrogenous base absent in DNA

questiontext.text: Which of the following bases is not present in DNA?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
DNA contains four nitrogenous bases: two purines (adenine and guanine) and two pyrimidines (cytosine and thymine).

Step 2: Evaluation
Uracil is a pyrimidine base found in RNA in place of thymine and is not present in DNA.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, uracil is not present in DNA.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q15 - Identifying anomers among three cyclic monosaccharide structures

questiontext.text:
Three cyclic structures of monosaccharides are given below which of these are anomers.

(I)

(II)

(III)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Three cyclic Fischer projections of monosaccharides are shown: two six-carbon pyranose structures (labeled I and II) and one seven-carbon cyclic structure (labeled III).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In cyclic Fischer projections of aldoses, the topmost ring carbon is \(\text{C}1\) (the anomeric hemiacetal carbon).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Anomers are cyclic diastereomers of a monosaccharide that differ in configuration exclusively at the anomeric carbon (\(\text{C}1\) for aldoses), while all other chiral centres retain identical configurations.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Comparing the first two cyclic structures: the first structure (\(\alpha\)-D-glucopyranose) has \(-\text{OH}\) on the right at \(\text{C}1\), while the second structure (\(\beta\)-D-glucopyranose) has \(-\text{OH}\) on the left at \(\text{C}1\). Their configurations at \(\text{C}2, \text{C}3, \text{C}4,\) and \(\text{C}5\) are identical. The third structure has a different carbon chain length and different configurations at multiple chiral centres, so it is neither an anomer of the first nor of the second structure.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Therefore, structures I and II are anomers.

answer.text: III is anomer of I and II

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q16 - Reaction explained only by cyclic structure of glucose

questiontext.text: Which of the following reactions of glucose can be explained only by its cyclic structure?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
While several reactions of glucose can be explained by its open-chain polyhydroxy aldehyde structure, certain reactions demonstrate the absence of a free \(-\text{CHO}\) group in its stable form.

Step 2: Evaluation
The formation of a pentaacetate confirms the presence of five \(-\text{OH}\) groups, reaction with hydroxylamine to form an oxime indicates a carbonyl group, and oxidation by nitric acid to gluconic/saccharic acid shows the presence of a primary alcohol and an aldehyde group—all consistent with the open-chain structure. However, the pentaacetate of glucose does not react with hydroxylamine, which proves that there is no free \(-\text{CHO}\) group in glucose pentaacetate because the \(\text{C}1\) carbon is locked in a cyclic hemiacetal (pyranose) ring.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the fact that pentaacetate of glucose does not react with hydroxylamine can be explained only by its cyclic structure.

answer.text: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime.
Pentaacetate of glucose does not react with hydroxylamine.
Glucose is oxidised by nitric acid to gluconic acid.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q17 - Determining D configuration from Fischer projections

questiontext.text:
Optical rotations of some compounds along with their structures are given below which of them have D configuration.

\((+)\) rotation

(I)

\((+)\) rotation

(II)

\((-)\) rotation

(III)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Three Fischer projections with their signs of optical rotation are shown: glyceraldehyde with \((+)\) rotation, glucose with \((+)\) rotation, and fructose with \((-)\) rotation.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The D/L nomenclature is a relative configuration system assigned by comparing the lowest asymmetric carbon atom in a standard Fischer projection (with the most oxidised carbon at the top) to glyceraldehyde. It is independent of the sign of optical rotation, \((+)\) or \((-)\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
If the \(-\text{OH}\) group on the lowest chiral carbon (the chiral carbon farthest from the carbonyl group) lies on the right-hand side in the Fischer projection, the sugar has the D configuration.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
In the glyceraldehyde structure, the chiral carbon \(\text{C}2\) has \(-\text{OH}\) on the right, so it has the D configuration. In the glucose structure, the lowest chiral carbon \(\text{C}5\) has \(-\text{OH}\) on the right, so it has the D configuration. In the fructose structure, even though its optical rotation is \((-)\), the lowest chiral carbon \(\text{C}5\) has \(-\text{OH}\) on the right, so it also has the D configuration.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
All three compounds (I, II, and III) have the D configuration.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q18 - Identifying anomeric carbon atoms in sucrose

questiontext.text: Structure of a disaccharide formed by glucose and fructose is given below. Identify anomeric carbon atoms in monosaccharide units.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The Haworth structure of sucrose is shown, consisting of an \(\alpha\)-D-glucopyranose ring (left) and a \(\beta\)-D-fructofuranose ring (right) joined by an \(-\text{O}-\) glycosidic bridge, with carbon atoms labeled 'a' through 'f' in each unit.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
An anomeric carbon is the carbonyl carbon of the open-chain sugar that becomes a new chiral centre (hemiacetal/acetal or hemiketal/ketal carbon) upon ring closure, and is bonded to two oxygen atoms (the ring oxygen and the exocyclic \(-\text{OH}\) or glycosidic oxygen).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
In aldohexoses (glucose), the aldehyde carbon is \(\text{C}1\). In ketohexoses (fructose), the ketone carbon is \(\text{C}2\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
In the glucose pyranose unit on the left, the carbon bonded to both the ring oxygen and the glycosidic oxygen is \(\text{C}1\), which is labeled 'a'. In the fructose furanose unit on the right, the carbon bonded to both the ring oxygen and the glycosidic oxygen (as well as the \(-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\) group labeled 'a') is \(\text{C}2\), which is labeled 'b'.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Therefore, the anomeric carbon atoms are the 'a' carbon of glucose and the 'b' carbon of fructose.

answer.text: 'a' carbon of glucose and 'a' carbon of fructose.
'a' carbon of glucose and 'e' carbon of fructose.
'a' carbon of glucose and 'b' carbon of fructose.
'f' carbon of glucose and 'f' carbon of fructose.
